view: This is the first report from a newly reorganized equity with no analyst coverage and a 75% resale overhang. Q3 will be split into predecessor and successor periods under fresh-start accounting, so the GAAP headline will be noisy and hard to compare. The disclosed trend points to another roughly 10-12% revenue decline and a steep fall in OIBDA. The price already holds that kind of decline: it sits near 3x trailing EBITDA after a 50% slide that has no fundamental news attached and looks like ex-creditor selling into the newly effective resale shelf. Neither direction has a datapoint I can show is missing from the price. There is no consensus to beat or miss. The release is an audio recording with no Q&A, and I found no executive remarks since emergence and no fresh third-party series on QxH or TikTok Shop for Q3. Two things also cut the scored window down. The 10-Q may well land after 13:00 ET, since the company's last post-petition 10-Q was filed at 14:25 ET, so much of the reaction may fall outside it. And continued selling by holders can swamp whatever the filing says. A big move in either direction is plausible, but I cannot see which way.

recommendation.reason: No consensus exists and I found no fresh third-party data on Q3 trading. The price already sits near 3x a falling EBITDA base after a supply-driven 50% decline, so I cannot name anything the market has missed in either direction. The filing time is unknown and may fall after the 13:00 ET exit, which weakens any signal further.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A 10-Q filed before the open that shows Q3 Adjusted OIBDA falling much less than the roughly 30% H1 pace, together with strong post-emergence cash and ABL availability, would make a long case. A sharper deceleration than Q2, or a going-concern or covenant warning, would make a short case.

self_critique: A newly reorganized equity at about 3x EBITDA with no coverage, falling on supply alone, is a classic setup for a sharp relief move once the first clean balance sheet and cash figure appear, and the 8.5% 5-day bounce on heavy volume could be early positioning for exactly that. Against that, an accelerating revenue decline with no Q&A could easily extend the slide. I cannot tell these apart with public data, so I stay at 50.
approach_notes: P4 (priced-in must be shown) helped: it pushed me to trace the 50% decline to the resale shelf and holder Form 4s rather than assume it was fundamental. P3's 'freshest data' had little to work on for a post-bankruptcy name with no coverage. The window rule, checked against filing timestamps, mattered as much as the fundamentals.
